entries.appliesTo: persons who knowingly publish, communicate, or distribute deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media within 90 days before a Vermont election

dutySources.disclosure-ui: § 2032(a) — 'unless the person includes a disclosure in the synthetic media stating:  "This media has been manipulated or generated by digital technology and depicts speech or conduct that did not occur."'

exposure.enforcer: attorney-general + state's-attorney; candidate private injunctive/equitable relief

sources.disclosure: § 2032(a) — 'A person shall not, within 90 days before an election in Vermont, publish, communicate, or otherwise distribute synthetic media that the person knows is deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media unless the person includes a disclosure in the synthetic media'
sources.scope: § 2032(a) — 'publish, communicate, or otherwise distribute synthetic media'
sources.windowDays: § 2032(a) — 'within 90 days before an election in Vermont'
sources.penaltyMax: § 2033(a)(3) — 'the person commits the violation with the intent to cause violence or bodily harm and the person commits the violation within five years after one or more prior violations under this section, in which case the fine shall be not more than $15,000.00'
sources.enforcer: § 2041 — 'a State's Attorney or the Attorney General may institute any appropriate action, injunction, or other proceeding to prevent, restrain, correct, or abate any violation of this chapter'; § 2033(b) — 'A candidate whose appearance, speech, conduct, or environment is misrepresented … may seek injunctive or other equitable relief'

flags: criminal-fine convention (rule 11): tiered fines — base $1,000 (§ 2033(a)); $5,000 with 'intent to cause violence or bodily harm' (§ 2033(a)(1)); $10,000 if 'within five years after one or more prior violations' (§ 2033(a)(2)); $15,000 if both (§ 2033(a)(3)); no imprisonment terms stated, but § 2042(a)(3) notes 'a knowing and intentional violation of this chapter is subject to criminal prosecution'
duty binds 'a person' generally, not only businesses — knowledge scienter required ('knows is deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media')

broad exceptions (§ 2032(b)): bona fide newscasts/news publications with authenticity acknowledgment, federally required candidate ads, satire or parody, telecommunications/information-service providers and interactive computer service providers (47 U.S.C. §§ 153, 230) for content provided by another person

detailed disclosure format specs (§ 2032(a)(1)-(2)): text 'easily readable' and shown 'for the full duration of the video recording'; audio disclosure at beginning, end, and at intervals of not greater than two minutes if audio exceeds two minutes
separate $5,000 fine for destroying/concealing/falsifying material to evade a civil investigation (§ 2042(b)(2))
Sec. 2 adds chapter-wide enforcement and civil-investigation powers (§§ 2041-2042: examination of records, testimony under oath, Superior Court enforcement petitions)
